meta.copy: Every line of copy and every citation here is checked at build time against scratchpad/sf-city-anim/entries/: a line on screen is a beat's own headline, or a verbatim run of a beat's quote, at the volume and BookReader leaf the shot cites. Two shots carry a DATA chip instead, because their source is a published register and an enacted ordinance rather than a scanned minute book, and they name it.
meta.geometry: Accepted centrelines: DataSF street centrelines, lit in the year the Board voted acceptance. The Bay Bridge west span: the same file, layer FREEWAYS, cnn 14248000 and 14249000. The 1942 district: the four streets the resolution itself names, clipped to the box of their own crossings.
meta.world: x and y are world DECIMETRES in the map's own frame — ((lon - proj.lon0) * proj.mpd * proj.cosl, (lat - proj.lat0) * proj.mpd), times ten.
meta.streets_note: The corpus opens in April 1906, so every street accepted before the fire was accepted before the record starts. 1,826 of the 2,051 are lit by 1930 and the last lands in 1947. Thirteen years in the span have no ingested volume, so the curve sits flat through them: that is the sweep, not the city.
meta.fire: The 1906 losses the first shot draws are a separate published file, film/fire.json, built by pipeline/scripts/us_sf_city/build_fire_losses.py.

title.head: San Francisco builds itself
title.sub: Eleven moments from the city's own record, 1906 to 2019

end.head: Every line in that film is a page you can open
end.sub: Stop anywhere and the map becomes the record: 45 entities, 2,051 accepted streets, 166,166 buildings.

shots.title: The fire, and what it took of the city's own
shots.copy: The fire burned for three days and destroyed some 28,000 buildings.

shots.title: It comes back
shots.copy: The city rebuilt more than it lost within nine years.

also.t: The city's own building permits — Municipal Reports, p. 367

shots.note: 28,559 new-building permits by June 1914, against 28,188 lost. Permits granted are not buildings completed, and the eight-year total is a sum of the city's own annual tables that none of them states.

shots.title: One building stays
shots.copy: San Francisco pulled down the Exposition's palaces when the fair closed and kept the Palace of Fine Arts.

shots.title: Two bridges
shots.copy: The Bay Bridge and the Golden Gate opened six months apart.

shots.title: Japantown
shots.copy: In 1942 the government removed everyone of Japanese descent from Japantown, and the Board's business for those streets that spring was property.

build.said: the district bounded by ELLIS, CALIFORNIA, GOUGH AND FILLMORE STREETS

shots.title: Fifty nations, in the war memorial
shots.copy: Fifty nations signed the United Nations Charter in the city's war memorial.

shots.title: The freeways that were not built
shots.copy: The Board rejected seven of the ten freeways the city had planned for San Francisco.

shots.title: The Pyramid
shots.copy: The Transamerica Pyramid was the tallest building in San Francisco for forty-six years.

links.t: 853 feet, fifty floors, 1972 — DataSF Tall Building Inventory
Salesforce Tower, 1,070 feet, opened 2018 — same register

shots.title: The road that came down
shots.copy: After the earthquake the Board voted to demolish the Embarcadero Freeway instead of repairing it.

shots.title: A rail yard becomes a neighbourhood
shots.copy: The Mission Bay rail yards became a neighbourhood of sixteen thousand people.

shots.title: What the city would not let itself do
shots.copy: San Francisco was the first city in America to tell its own police they could not use facial recognition.

links.t: Ordinance No. 103-19, File 190110, finally passed 10 to 1 on 21 May 2019
